Abhishek Sharma Ascends to ICC No.1 T20 Batting Rank After 113‑Run Blitz

04 Nov 2026, 10:29 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.inextlive.com

2 min read

Summary

Abhishek Sharma vaulted to the top of the ICC Men’s T20 batting rankings on Wednesday, overtaking fellow Indian Ishaan Kishan. The move follows Sharma’s explosive 113‑run innings off just 38 balls against New Zealand in the third T20 International of the series, a knock that helped India win by six wickets.

Match Highlights

  • Opponent: New Zealand
  • Series: 5‑match T20I bilateral series (India hosted)
  • Date: 27 May 2024 (local time, India)
  • Result: India won by 6 wickets
  • Sharma’s innings: 113 runs from 38 balls (12 fours, 9 sixes)
  • Impact: Secured India’s fourth‑innings chase and contributed to a series‑leveling win.

Ranking Shift

Source-listed details
RankPlayer (Team)Rating Points
1Abhishek Sharma (India)897
2Farhan (Pakistan) – T20 captain883
3Ishaan Kishan (India)866
9Shreyas Iyer (India) – fell five places758

*Why the change?* Sharma’s 113 boosted his rating by a large margin, while Kishan missed the second and third T20s of the series due to injury, causing his points to slip. Farhan’s consistent performances kept him in the top three, and Iyer’s recent dip in form resulted in a five‑place drop.

What It Means for Teams

  • India: Having a world‑number‑one T20 batter strengthens the middle order and gives the side a psychological edge in upcoming tournaments, such as the ICC T20 World Cup 2024.
  • Pakistan: Farhan’s hold on the second spot underscores the depth of Pakistan’s batting talent and may influence squad selections for the next series.
  • Other Nations: The shift highlights how a single innings can dramatically reshape the rankings, reminding teams to manage player workloads and injury risks.

How to Verify

The ICC publishes weekly ranking updates on its official website (icc-cricket.com/rankings). The specific update dated 28 May 2024 lists the points shown above. Match details, including Sharma’s 113, are recorded in the official scorecard for the India vs New Zealand 3rd T20I on the same site.
